scores.evidence: T8–T14 can run in parallel against the contract once T5 merges.
scores.rationale: Order runs contract/repo/infra/CI, then service components, then load, then shadow, enforcement and rollout; dependencies and spike gates are explicit.

scores.evidence: M1: Working slice + spikes ... staging on EKS ... Out: prod
scores.rationale: M1 is a real end-to-end slice with load test and Athena-queryable decisions, but it runs in staging on synthetic traffic and excludes prod, so it isn't a prod path.

scores.evidence: D1 ... Hard (Auth Host integration) ... Revisit if: The Auth Host can't give ≥ 30 ms.
scores.rationale: The plan has an assumptions table and a decision table with options, reversibility and revisit triggers, plus open questions with defaults.

scores.evidence: Order: start T1–T4 on day 1, because they are long-lead. T5–T7 come next.
scores.rationale: Widest-impact work (contract, accounts, repo skeleton, infra) comes first and shared libs before leaves, but the plan doesn't frame this as blast-radius ordering.

scores.evidence: T2 Submit the PCI scope review ... T8 mTLS, request checks (reject unknown fields) ... T10 tampered bundle is rejected
scores.rationale: Security shows up concretely in M1 (mTLS, signed bundles, Trivy, KMS, PCI review) and in M2 (parity tests, Lake Formation) and M3 (game days); it also appears in the rollout.

scores.evidence: T17 Add the dashboard and alerts ... Injected 50 ms latency in staging triggers the alert
scores.rationale: M1 includes per-stage timers, OTel, dashboards and alerts, and later milestones add paging, model-health metrics and reconciliation.

scores.evidence: Applied only through the pipeline; `terraform plan` shows no drift; remote state with locking
scores.rationale: Terraform, pinned CI builds and tagged images, signed versioned artefacts, Replay Harness and logged feature vectors, and decision reproducibility are built in from M1.

scores.evidence: T14 Implement the degraded path: 10 ms Redis timeout, circuit breaker, missing-feature flags, `degraded=true`
scores.rationale: Failure handling is in M1 (degraded path, failover load test, Kafka buffer), M2 (fallback tests) and M3 (game days and rebuild drill).

scores.evidence: Guardrails: thresholds bounded ... decline-rate band with automatic canary rollback ... Human approval: Fraud Risk signs off every model promotion
scores.rationale: Guardrails, human sign-off and monitor-only mode precede enforcement, but the plan has no explicit budgets and no retrieval/memory/orchestration/routing layers (not needed for a GBDT system); its ordering is sensible but not in the rubric's order.

scores.evidence: Rule-authoring UI ... Trigger: Analysts take more than 1 day per rule because of Git friction
scores.rationale: The deferred table gives pull-forward triggers, and the plan also lists deliberate shortcuts with payback conditions and the M1 placeholders.

note: This is a strong, thorough plan: its gaps are a staging-only Phase 0 (no prod walking skeleton) and no explicit AI budgets or layer ordering.
